Definition: from G2532 and G5104; and yet, i.e. nevertheless:--although.
BiblicalUsage: Kaitoi is 'and yet' — the word that holds a concession and a contradiction together. God left not Himself without witness, and yet He gave rain and fruitful seasons; and the works were finished from the foundation of the world, and yet some did not enter into rest.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that 'and yet' is the shape of faith: God has spoken and God has provided, and yet men still refuse — and the fault is never His.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
